correctness.rationale: The exact unit interval squared-difference law has moments 1/6,1/15,1/28 and nonzero cumulants 1/6,7/180,11/945. Three independent scaled copies yield the first three power sums of squared sides, and Newton identities yield the cubic. With fixed p1,p2, the normalized squared sides lie on a circle in the positive simplex. The product has precisely the two-positive-two-equal stationary profiles, with boundary zero only when q>=1/2; their explicit products give the complete range. Feasibility follows by continuity. The first two moments have explicit noncongruent profiles. Exact SymPy checks and numerical tests passed using the actual included script. The analytic proof (not numerical trials) covers all positive edge lengths and all feasible parameter values.

originality.rationale: Forward point-pair distances for boxes are known from Philip (2007), and forward cube moment theory from Mathai et al. (1999); the novel claim is the *three-moment minimal inverse* with exact sharp conditional feasible volume envelope and its lower-endpoint transition. Full distance-law rigidity is not claimed separately. Geometric object and sampling law differ from closest published flat-torus, triangle, or parallelogram inverse results and from the billiard line-intercept inverse. Author-site full primary text shows forward convolutions and explicit breakpoints, but no three-even-moment volume envelope; historical completeness remains provisional.
residual_risks: The full 1999 Mathai–Moschopoulos–Pederzoli text was not retrieved; abstract covers forward cube moments only.

value.rationale: The exact feasible moment region gives quantitative sharp bounds on the three-dimensional volume using only second and fourth distance moments and says exactly when the lower bound is attained versus merely approached. The third even moment completely resolves shape, with generic optimality. This is a natural inverse geometric probability question motivated by the older forward box-distance formulas; the two distinct isosceles-type equality classes and q=1/2 transition are nontrivial geometric output, not merely rescaling a known cube moment.
